absent: Lifetime and teardown of hyp identity mappings beyond initial text mapping.
Update protocol and invalidation for the compressed MPIDR lookup table.
Detection criteria for direct MSI capability and ITS hardware compatibility.
Emulated LPI injection and queuing behavior when direct forwarding is not used.
Hyp mode setup, vector slot management, subsystem bringup and VMID allocation details.
Full register table contents and nested trap forwarding actions.
Handling of SVE register slices for vector lengths beyond the architectural limit.
Host interrupt chip state synchronization guarantees beyond pending latch migration.

findings.text: Provides lookup from masked hardware MPIDR affinity to the corresponding vCPU within a VM, returning null when no vCPU matches. An accelerated RCU protected table is consulted first with validation of the candidate, otherwise a full vCPU scan is used as fallback.

Exposes hooks for irq bypass producers and routing updates plus a predicate for in-kernel irqchip presence. Only message-signalled routing entries are eligible for direct forwarding; other types complete successfully without action. Routing changes to an identical message entry are ignored, otherwise direct state is released to allow software injection.

Offers establishment and teardown of direct message interrupt forwarding to virtual LPIs. Establishment succeeds silently without state change when direct handling is unsupported or the routing does not resolve to a usable virtual interrupt, allowing emulated injection to continue. Teardown releases any host association for the given host interrupt.

Resolves message-signalled transactions to virtual ITS state and then to a target virtual interrupt. Doorbell addresses are accepted only when they land on a registered GIC device of ITS type; device and event identifiers require valid device data and a mapped collection with LPIs enabled on the target vCPU.
Provides hypervisor address size selection and identity mapping of hypervisor text as executable. Mapping failures are reported through the error log path with the status propagated to the caller.

Hypervisor stage one must cover both its own identity code and all kernel memory with a single table base, so its address width is the larger of the identity width and the active kernel stage one width.
A collection counts as mapped only when its handle exists and its target address differs from the designated unmapped sentinel.
LPIs are considered enabled for a vCPU exactly when its redistributor control state holds the enable LPIs value.
Translation cache indexing combines device identity and event identity into one key with device identity occupying the high portion shifted by the platform typer width.

Translation caching is best effort and never applies to directly injected interrupts. Insertion requires exclusive ITS ownership, holds a reference while cached, tolerates store failures by dropping the new reference, and releases any prior entry displaced by a race.

Invalid guest or userspace interrupt configurations do not fail forwarding setup; they leave hardware state untouched and report success so that software LPI delivery remains available if the guest later corrects itself.

Direct forwarding serializes ITS membership changes with a sleepable ITS mutex held across resolution and mapping, while per-interrupt hardware association and pending state are protected by a raw spinlock taken with interrupts saved. The spinlock is always nested inside the mutex; teardown uses only the spinlock plus reference handling.

MPIDR table and host to virtual interrupt reverse lookups run under RCU read protection with reference acquisition before use. Doorbell to ITS translation runs under SRCU protection for I/O bus stability. Cache insertion asserts exclusive ITS ownership.

Direct mapping descriptors carry the owning VM interrupt state, the target virtual processing element, the virtual interrupt number, property bits derived from priority together with enabled and group attributes, and a doorbell enable flag.

ITS software state organizes devices by identifier, each owning interrupt translation entries keyed by event identifier, with each entry pointing to a collection and a virtual interrupt. Collections resolve to a vCPU through their stored target address.

Each virtual LPI has a direct flag that is clear when emulated and set when forwarded, paired with a host interrupt number and a per-processor-element counter. Establishment sets the flag and count and migrates any latched pending state to the host; teardown clears the flag, decrements the count and releases the host mapping.

ITS translation distinguishes disabled ITS, unknown device or event, unmapped collection, missing vCPU target, and disabled LPIs as failure outcomes that prevent delivery of a virtual interrupt reference.

System initialization aborts when hypervisor mode is unavailable or administratively disabled, otherwise prepares register tables, address limits, vector extensions and VM identity allocation before hypervisor and subsystem setup and core registration, finalizing protected state only on success and unwinding prior allocations on any failure.

Register table setup validates ordering and uniqueness of all architectural tables including the GIC extension, then initializes implementation-defined registers, nested trap forwarding, feature coverage checks and per-register configuration, failing if any table is malformed or any configuration step fails.

Intermediate physical address width derives from the sanitized PARANGE field, capped to a smaller width when large addressing is unavailable for the active page size, and rejected when the active page size lacks stage two support or reports an unknown granularity value.

When scalable vectors are supported, guest maximum vector length comes from the virtualizable limit clamped to the architectural maximum, with the host maximum recorded separately including for non-VHE hyp use, and a warning issued when heterogeneity forces guests below the host maximum.

Feature description tables must account for every bit that is not architecturally reserved, excluding only architectural forced-reserved bits from coverage; any uncovered or unexpected bit is reported as undefined behavior for the associated control.

Nested trap forwarding builds a shared encoding database for coarse and fine traps, rejecting reserved control values, duplicate encodings, invalid groups, reserved fine bits and recursive multi-control combinations, and discards the database if any inconsistency is detected.
Routing updates that arrive in atomic context cannot sleep for new translation resolution, so any material message change only tears down direct state and relies on software injection thereafter.
Bypass lifecycle transitions halt the guest when forwarding stops and resume it when forwarding starts, coupling host interrupt path changes to guest execution state.
Systems advertising certain device load-acquire errata warn that guests lacking required workarounds may deadlock the system and should be restricted to trusted images.
Identity mapping uses a fixed width of 48 address bits.
Doorbell translation succeeds only for addresses that resolve on the MMIO bus to a GIC operations device whose type marks an ITS instance; all other addresses yield an invalid doorbell error.
Message translation requires ITS support in the VM and a valid device identifier flag in the message; the doorbell address is formed from high and low address halves.
Host to virtual reverse lookup scans the LPI address space for an entry already marked direct with matching host number and acquires a reference only on success.
